check.verdict: PASS WITH MINOR DEFECTS. Row indices below are 0-based positions in the JSON array (row 0 = "17 September 2014"). Structure is clean: the JSON has 51 rows, exactly matching the 51 German table rows (headers on source lines 4-5, 53-54, 106-107 correctly dropped), and the order is identical. No cell is shifted between rows or columns - every date/article/action/addressee/note quadruple sits where the German has it, including the multi-line wrapped rows (e.g. source lines 59-63, 64-68, 120-122) and the "-" placeholders in row 7. A token-level diff of all numerals shows a perfect match: every article, paragraph, annex (V, VI, VII) and Implementing Regulation number (2015/806, 2015/1502, 2015/1505, 2015/1506, 2025/2162, 2025/2530, 2025/1943) is unchanged, and the multi-article cells (27(5)/37(5); 50(1)/52(2); 31(3)/32(3)/32a(3)/33(2)/34(2); 42(2)/44(2)/45(2)/45j(2)/45l(3); 9(3)/9(4)/5d(6)/31(1); 5c(4)/12a(3)/30(3a); 26(2)/36(2); 5e(2)/10(3)) are complete and in source order. All 34 dates are converted correctly and unambiguously from DD.MM.YYYY to spelled-out month form - no day/month transposition (checked especially 01.07.2015, 01.07.2016, 18.03.2025, 20.05.2024). Defined terms follow the glossary: "Wallet" is consistently expanded to "European Digital Identity Wallet" (#42), "vertrauende Beteiligte" to "relying parties" (#6), "Identitaetsabgleich" to "identity matching" (#55), "Journalen" to "ledgers" (#52), "authentische Quellen" to "authentic sources" (#47), "Attributsbescheinigungen" to "attestations of attributes" (#44/45), "Vertrauensdiensteanbieter" to "trust service providers" (#19). Substantive wording checked against the official English also holds: Art 51(1)-(4), 5a(1) ("each Member State shall provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet"), 5f(2) (36 months, "microenterprises and small enterprises"), 5f(5) ("the demand for, and the availability and usability of"), 20(1)/(1a) ("at their own expense", "three working days", "one month before any planned audits"), 21(2) (three months / two-month NIS2 response), 24(1c) ("verification of identity and attributes"), 24(2)(a) (one month / three months), 24(2)(fb) and 24(3) (24 hours), 5c(4)/12a(3) (five years, biennial vulnerability assessment, three-month remediation), 6(1) (12 months), 7(g) (six months), 26(2)/36(2), 48a, 52(2)(a)/(b). Two terminology defects remain, both in the "action" column; neither affects a number, date or row placement.

defects.problem: "gegenseitigen Begutachtung (Peer Review)" is rendered as "mutual assessment (peer review)". "Mutual assessment" is not the official English term: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 Art 12(5)/(6) uses German "gegenseitige Begutachtungen" for English "peer reviews" ("the necessary procedural arrangements for the peer reviews referred to in paragraph 5"). The invented term plus the parenthetical gloss is redundant and breaks the one-to-one mapping to the official vocabulary.
defects.correction: Implementing Regulation on the procedural arrangements for the peer reviews

defects.problem: "Zuruecknahme des eID-Systems" is rendered as "revocation of the eID scheme". The official English of Art 10(3) for German "Zurücknahme des elektronischen Identifizierungssystems" is "withdrawal of the electronic identification scheme". "Revocation" is the official English for a different German verb in the same article (Art 10(1) "widerruft" = "revoke", which applies to the cross-border authentication, not to the scheme), so the choice both departs from the official term and blurs two distinct legal acts.
defects.correction: At the latest after three months without remedy: withdrawal of the European Digital Identity Wallet or withdrawal of the eID scheme
